recipes.name: Cheesy Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 1 pound frozen Southern-style hash brown potatoes
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of potato soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix potatoes, condensed soup, and sour cream together in a large baking dish; mix in cheese, butter, salt, and pepper to taste. Top mixture with potato chips.
Bake in the preheated oven until the mixture is bubbly and lightly brown, about 1 hour.
Remove from oven and let stand 15 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These cheesy potatoes are easy to make with Southern-style hash brown potatoes, sour cream, and Cheddar cheese for a creamy potato casserole.

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe for years to rave reviews, with a couple of adjustments. I always put in a 2 lb. bag of hash browns instead of the 1 lb. that is called for here. Also I use cream of celery or cream of mushroom soup instead of cream of potato. Finally I add the crushed corn flakes mixed with a little butter on top to give it a little crispy topping and this is my holiday potato recipe. The best part is that it can be made ahead of time, like the day before (keep refrigerated), which is a big plus at holidays. Just don't put the crushed corn flakes/butter on top until ready to bake.

This recipe was really good, almost tasted like my "loaded maashed potatoes. It was great with a few modifications: I peeled my own potatoes instead of using frozen has browns (about 9) and boiled them on the stove in water for about 30-45 minutes. Once they were cooked and drained, I mixed all of the ingredients together and substituted a can of cream of mushroom for cream of potato. I also added bacon bits and salt and pepper to the mixture. I only had to bake them for about 20-25 minutes since the potatoes had been boiled. Really delish!

Hope this helps!

This is a good side dish. I did make a few modifications though. I didn't use all of the cheese that was suggested. 16oz seemed like quite a bit. I mixed 8 oz in with the potatoes and sprinkled about 1/2 cup on top. In addition, I mixed in 1/2 cup each of onions and green peppers. I omitted the potato chips. Delicious!

I used the basic recipe here with a few changes. I boiled 10 raw potatoes in water, cubed, for 30 minuites. Then drained and added to pan with cheese, cream of mushroom soup and sour cream (8 oz). I topped with cheese, bacon bits and potato chips. This received rave reviews from kids and adults alike! Thanks for a really nice crowd pleaser!

Although i have not tried the way the recipe reads i didn’t want to risk it and made some changes to procedure and ingredients which made it a5+ star recipe! I used real potatoes and cut them into small cubes. Importantly , i brought the water to a boil then threw in the potatoes (i believe his helped keep them together and not mushy) and pulled them just as they became soft. I used a handful of left over fancy aged and seasoned brine cheese i had from a party and grated that up along with a little cheddar for the base mix. What really put this over the top i believe is i used about a half stick of cream cheese as well as replace 1/4 cup of milk with heavy cream. I mixed these all together to make a mix then spread half the mix over the bottom of the casserole pan then threw the potatoes on top of that and folded the rest of the mix into the potatoes. This totally helped with coating them. Lastly i used corn flake bread crumbs instead of potato chips and then topped that with just cheddar cheese. The topping was crispy and creamy. I can’t wait to make this again. I think i might add salsa next time or taco seasoning for a twist! All credit to the original creator who has an excellent recipe!
Adjusted recipe a bit. Added 2 lbs of hashbrown potatoes and a can of cream of mushroom soup. Huge hit!!
Great dish - brought it for a Holiday party at work and everyone loved it. I recommend using half the amount of butter and extra potatoes.

1st time i made this was to bring to a Christmas party. I followed the recipe but I didn't use the potato chips and it was very good and got many compliments, but I thought it tasted a little to much of sour cream. The next time I made it I only use about 1/2 the amount of the sour cream and it tasted so much better and got so many more compliments. This is an awesome dish and a crowd pleaser. Their is NEVER any left over.

I liked this, though I wish there had been a higher potato vs. other stuff ratio. It was a little too saucy for me. I think I would use twice or half as much more potatoes next time. Also, I found the butter to be unneccessary; the grease from the cheese and the water from the potatoes seemed to provide plenty of liquid. I left off the potato chips and topped it with more cheese, which I allowed to melt and form a crust. I think you could make a "lower fat" version of this if you used low fat soup, cheese, and sour cream, etc... All in all, a good recipe.

I read the reviews carefully before starting this and I chose to use 2 pounds of hash browns. Good call. This turned out really good and made excellent leftovers for breakfast at work. The one thing that I didn't care for was the cream of potato soup. The potatoes in the soup had a different texture and took on a different flavor profile from the hash browns and not in a great way. I recommend using cream of celery or mushroom instead. Overall great recipe with a couple small tweaks.

I made this recipe in order to use up a half bag of frozen hash browns I had. I had less than 14oz of hash browns to put towards this recipe and I do agree with others, a full 2lb bag would probably be better -- I only put 12oz of cheese because 16oz did seem like a lot (and that's coming from a cheese addict) -- I used a 14oz can of semi-condensed cream of mushroom soup which probably contributed to the more soupy consistency, however I think this would have been totally fine with using 2lbs of potatoes -- the butter is totally pointless in my opinion, there's enough grease from the cheese, sour cream and soup to omit this -- I didn't top it with the chips since I was portioning this out for the week and couldn't afford the calories. Over all a tasty dish, if I make it again I will increase the potatoes to 2lbs and omit the butter.
Very good
I made it for Christmas . Delicious I have made this before I only use cheddar cheese soup.
So good! Follow the recipe as is, can't go wrong!
I made this for dinner tonight, based on reviews I cut the butter to 1/4 cup, and added more potatoes. This was dry.
I made it without potato chips and butter. Did 2lbs of potatoes; two cans of cream of potato soup. Came out delish for the Christmas ham.
recipe was easy and good.
Super good! Would recommend!!!!!!
Amazing! Love it.

the 1st time i made it i followed the recipe to the tee except i didn't use the crushed potato chips and it was good but it tasted to much of sour cream, I'm not a big fan of sour cream. the 2nd time i used half the sour cream it was awesome! thanks for the recipe, its one of my favorite side dishes to make and every year at the company christmas party everybody always ask if i can bring it.
